'''Tormod Næs''' (born February 11, 1954{{Citation needed|date=April 2023}}) is a Norwegian statistician working in [[chemometrics]] and [[sensometrics]]. He studies [[Multivariate statistics|multivariate statistical analysis]], [[spectroscopy]], [[food science]], and sensory science. His impact on chemometrics is exemplified by the over 8,000 citations to his most well-known book, ''Multivariate Calibration'' (with Harald Martens),<ref>{{Cite web |title=[BOOK] Multivariate Calibration H Martens, T Naes |year=1992 |url=https://scholar.google.com/scholar?hl=en&as_sdt=0%2C34&q=%5BBOOK%5D+Multivariate+calibration+H+Martens%2C+T+Naes+-+1992+&btnG= |website=Google Scholar}}</ref> and the awards in chemometrics that he has received.

== Education ==
Tormod Næs obtained both his master's degree (1978) and PhD (1984) in statistics from [[University of Oslo]].<ref name=":5">{{Cite web |title=Tormod Næs |url=http://www.ntva.no/medlemmer/tormod-naes/ |access-date=2023-04-04 |website=NTVA |language=nb-NO}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Tormod Naes |url=https://nofima.com/employee/tormod-naes/  |access-date=March 31, 2023 |website=Nofima|date=May 26, 2021 }}</ref>

== Career ==
For most of his career Næs has worked at [[Norwegian Food Research Institute|Nofima]] (Norwegian Food Research institute) at [[Ås, Viken|Ås]], achieving the title of Senior Scientist.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":7">{{Cite journal |date= |title=SU partners with overseas research institute to study 'drivers of liking' |url=https://academic.sun.ac.za/wine_biotechnology/HOME/N%20E%20W%20S.pdf |journal=Stellenbosch University / Campus News / Kampusnuus |issue=June/July 2009}}</ref> He has been a professor at the University of Oslo, the [[University of Copenhagen]], and  [[Stellenbosch University]].<ref name=":5" /> Næs has had four long research and guest professor periods abroad; at [[University of Washington]] (Seattle), [[University of Delaware]], [[University of Genoa|University of Genova]] and [[University of Florence|University of Firenze]].{{Citation needed|date=April 2023}}

Næs was member of The Board of Directors, Matforsk (now Nofima) for four years, chairman of the ''8th Sensometrics Conference'': ''Imagine the Senses'', held August 2006 in [[Ås, Viken|Ås]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Past Conferences |url=https://sensometric.wildapricot.org/conference  |access-date=April 1, 2023 |website=The Sensometric Society}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |title=Special Issue: 8th Sensometrics Meeting Matforsk, Norway, [at Ås, Norway During August of 2006] |publisher=Elsevier |year=2006 |editor-last=Næs |editor-first=Tormod |via=Google Books}}</ref> chairman of the organising committee for the ''‘PLS’07: 5th International Symposium on PLS and Related Methods'' (September 2007)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Simplified version of conference home page |url=https://marcia.iqm.unicamp.br/Mnotes19.html  |access-date=March 31, 2023 |website=marcia.iqm.unicamp.br/Mnotes19.html}}</ref> and chairman of the ''16th Scandinavian Symposium on Chemometrics'' (''SSC16''): ''Chemometrics in Action'' (June 2019).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Scandinavian Symposium on Chemometrics (SSC) |url=https://ssc16.org/  |access-date=March 31, 2023 |website=The SSC16 conference}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Committees |url=https://ssc16.org/scientific-committee/  |access-date=March 31, 2023 |website=The SSC16 conference}}</ref>

During his time at Nofima, Næs has been project and task leader of a number of research projects financed by [[Research Council of Norway]] and EU (Marie Curie). Among these was "ConsumerCheck," a four-year (2009–2012) international project which involved researchers working in collaboration with Nofima from their home bases in South Africa, Denmark, and the Netherlands.<ref name=":7" /> [https://consumercheck.co/ Consumercheck website] Næs headed the project "RapidCheck" at Nofima. This was a project which studied rapid method for food producers to test their products and to understand better why consumers eat what they eat.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Boge |first=Lidunn Mosaker |date=April 3, 2016 |title=Learn to taste yourself |url=https://nofima.com/results/learn-to-taste-yourself/ |access-date=2023-04-07 |website=Nofima |language=en-US}}</ref> Næs served as the project leader for "Panelcheck" for eight months (September 1, 2007–May 5, 2007).<ref>{{Cite web |title=PanelCheck Navigation - News |url=https://www.panelcheck.com/Home/panelcheck_news |access-date=2023-04-07 |website=www.panelcheck.com |language=en-US}}</ref> PanelCheck is a well established open source software package of multiple statistical and graphical tools used within the field of sensometrics for performance analysis of trained sensory panels.<ref>{{Cite arXiv |last1=Tomic |first1=Oliver |last2=Kuznetsova |first2=Alexandra |last3=Bruun Brockhoff |first3=Per |last4=Graff |first4=Thomas |last5=Næs |first5=Tormod |date=January 12, 2022 |title=ConsumerCheck: A Software for Analysis of Sensory and Consumer Data |class=cs.HC |eprint=2201.04020 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Tomic |first1=Oliver |last2=Luciano |first2=Giorgio |last3=Nilsen |first3=Asgeir |last4=Hyldig |first4=Grethe |last5=Lorensen |first5=Kirsten |last6=Næs |first6=Tormod |date=2009 |title=Analysing sensory panel performance in a proficiency test using the PanelCheck software |url=https://www.academia.edu/80473954 |journal=European Food Research and Technology |volume=230 |issue=3 |pages=497 |doi=10.1007/s00217-009-1185-y |s2cid=95322533 |issn=1438-2377 |access-date=April 7, 2023 |via=Academia.edu}}</ref> It was developed by researchers at MATFORSK (Norwegian Food Research Institute), the Technical University of Denmark (DTU) and the University of Copenhagen.<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://documentation.help/PanelCHECK/documentation.pdf |title=PanelCheck Manual |year=2006}}</ref>

Næs has been European editor of ''Journal of Chemometrics'' (2003–2005)<ref name=":6">{{Cite journal |last=Brown |first=Steven |date=April 2003 |title=Editorial |journal=Journal of Chemometrics |language=en |volume=17 |issue=4 |pages=199 |doi=10.1002/cem.798|s2cid=221550366 |doi-access=free }}</ref> and served as associate editor of ''[[Technometrics]]'' (2007–2008).<ref>{{Cite journal |date=February 2008 |title=Front Matter |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/25471417 |journal=Technometrics |volume=50 |issue=1 |issn=0040-1706 |jstor=25471417}}</ref> He is currently (as of 2023) on the editorial board of ''[[Food Quality and Preference]]'',<ref>{{Cite journal |title=Editorial Board |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/food-quality-and-preference/about/editorial-board |journal=Food Quality and Preference |publisher=Elsevier |access-date=March 31, 2023 |via=Science Direct}}</ref> ''Journal of Chemometrics''<ref>{{Cite journal |date=2023 |title=Editorial Board |url=https://analyticalsciencejournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/hub/journal/1099128x/homepage/editorialboard.html |journal=Journal of Chemometrics |publisher=John Wiley & Sons |doi=10.1002/(ISSN)1099-128X |access-date=March 31, 2023|url-access=subscription }}</ref> and ''Italian Journal of Applied Statistics'' (''Statistica Applicata'').<ref>{{Cite journal |title=Editorial board |url=https://www.sa-ijas.org/rivista/en/editorial.html |journal=Statistica Applicata (Italian Journal of Applied Statistics) |access-date=March 31, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |title=Editorial Team |url=https://www.sa-ijas.org/ojs/index.php/sa-ijas/about/editorialTeam |journal=Statistica Applicata (Italian Journal of Applied Statistics) |publisher=Elsevier |access-date=March 31, 2023}}</ref>

Næs has supervised 24 PhD students to their final degree.<ref name=":5" />

== Influence and recognition ==
Tormod Næs has a large production of scientific papers and books and has an h-index (as of March 2023) equal to 48 in Web of Science and equal to 66 in Google Scholar.{{Citation needed|date=April 2023}} He is particularly known to researchers in chemometrics for his ability to combine multivariate statistics with applied areas in spectroscopy and sensory science, in this way building bridges between these areas.<ref name=":6" />

Næs and Tomas Isaksson received the Thomas Hirshfeld Award in NIR Analysis, given by the International Council for Near Infrared Spectroscopy (ICNIRS) to recognize contributions to [[Near-infrared spectroscopy|NIR spectroscopy]], in 1997.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=2019 Tomas Hirschfeld Award |url=https://www.spectroscopyeurope.com/news/2019-tomas-hirschfeld-award  |access-date=March 31, 2023 |website=Spectroscopy Europe/World|date=May 7, 2019 }}</ref> In their award address, Isaksson spoke about the role of NIR spectroscopy in [[food quality]], and Næs spoke about the use of [[principal component analysis]], [[Linear least squares|least squares regression]], and [[Euclidean distance]] or [[Mahalanobis distance]] in chemometrics.<ref name=":1" />

In 1997 Næs was awarded the Eastern Analytical Symposium (EAS) Award for Outstanding Achievements in Chemometrics,<ref name=":3" /> an award that recognizes [[analytical chemists]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2023 EAS Awards |url=https://eas.org/?page_id=2142  |access-date=March 31, 2023 |website=Eastern Analytical Symposium}}</ref>

In 2012 Næs and coauthors O. Tomic, B. H. Mevik, and H. Martens received the Kowalski Prize from the ''Journal of Chemometrics'' for their paper "Path modelling by sequential PLS regression" (2011).<ref name=":4" />
